MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 22, 2026
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum at
5:00 p.m., on September 22, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
p.m. on September 17, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  Tarquin Preziosi, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Alison Walker, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

 At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Bucknum recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:00 pm Mayor
 Bucknum reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  September 22, 2026
  PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognition of 50th Anniversary of the 1976 Olympics

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamations to Olympians Wendy Burge and Brian Goodell.

 P2.  Recognition of Nadadores Dive and Swim Athletes

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates to the Nadadores national dive and swim athletes and
  their coaches.

 P3.  Business Spotlight - Wineworks/Dublin 4

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to Darren Coyle, owner of Wineworks/Dublin 4.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Raised concerns about inconsistent enforcement of speaking limits and privacy
risks from Flock license plate readers, urging caution.

Gene Dery, M.V.: Questioned high overtime in the Public Service Department and lack of explanation.

Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Expressed concern over the lack of transparency and public input on
surveillance camera installations, citing constitutional rights.

Andie Lofy, M.V.: Warned about mass surveillance from Flock’s AI technology and potential law
enforcement misuse.

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: Director of the Moulton Niguel Water District and candidate for re-election,
highlighted his focus on cooperation and infrastructure for reliable water service.

Whitney White, M.V.: Honored the City Council and shared a call to foster unity, spiritual virtues, and
collaboration to strengthen the diverse community, offering a resource titled "A Common Endeavor" to
support this goal.

Faith Fersten, M.V.: Thanked the city for recently cleaning up a neighboring hoarder’s property but
expressed concern that the occupant is starting to accumulate items again, creating an eyesore.

William Palma, M.V.: Expressed frustration with limited impact of public comments and detailed
ongoing legal actions against the Orange County Sheriff’s Department for records violations, involving
the U.S. Department of Justice.

Paola Trumbly, M.V.: Invited the community to join Love Our School Day on October 10, a joint effort
to support local schools through volunteer projects and a luncheon celebration.

City Council Minutes  2  September 22, 2026
 Robert Breton, M.V.: Praised Mission Viejo’s effective homelessness strategy, emphasizing prevention,
dedicated outreach staff, and nonprofit partnerships, which led to a 50% drop in unsheltered
homelessness last year.

Angela Ponticelli, M.V.: Requested a city pilot program to support homeschool groups with access to
facilities, emphasizing the growing homeschool community and a desire for partnership. She also
commended Mayor Bucknum’s responsiveness.

Lauren McKinley, M.V.: Urged the city to provide a consistent, distraction-free space for homeschool
groups and supported the pilot program request.

Karlee Messenger, M.V.: Highlighted the homeschool co-op’s community and civic benefits and
supported the pilot program to foster a partnership with the city.

Cathy Palmer, M.V. (Zoom): Supported opposition to Flock cameras, raised concerns about high public
works overtime, and urged balanced funding for parks and libraries. She also encouraged using Zoom
to increase public participation.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 9 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell to approve Items 1
through 8 of the Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of September 8, 2026, as
  presented.

 2.  General Check Register Dated August 28 & September 4, 2026

  Ratified the accompanying check registers.

 3.  Golf Check Register dated August 28 & September 4, 2026

  Ratified the accompanying check registers.

 4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2026

City Council Minutes  3  September 22, 2026
   Received and filed.

 5.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for July 2026

  Received and filed.

 6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2026

  Received and filed.

 7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2026

  Received and filed.

 8.  Purchase one (1) 2027 Ford F-350 Animal Services Vehicle Replacement and
  appropriate funding for one (1) Animal Shelter Facility Wastewater Pump Replacement

  (1) Awarded a Purchase Agreement for one (1) 2027 Ford F-350 SRW XL to 72 Hour LLC,
  DBA National Auto Fleet Group in an amount not to exceed $59,846; (2) awarded a Purchase
  Agreement for one (1) Six Compartment Chassis Mount Animal Control Unit with outfitted
  accessories to Deerskin Manufacturing, Inc. (A26-30) in an amount not to exceed $73,444;
  and (3) adopted Resolution 26-47 amending the Animal Services Fund Fiscal Year 2026/27
  Budget to appropriate $163,098 from available fund balance for the Animal Services vehicle
  replacement and Animal Services facility wastewater pump replacement.

 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 9.  Council Member Kelley wanted to highlight this item for the community.

  Mayor Bucknum asked for any council questions.

  There were no requests to speak on this item.

  Council Members provided comments.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve
  and authorize the Assistant City Manager to execute the County of Orange Agreement and
  Authorize Staff to Accept the $100,000 Contribution for the City’s Sports and Events
  Tourism Efforts.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  September 22, 2026
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

 10.  Continued Public Hearing to Consider General Plan Amendment P-GPA2026-0005 /
  Zone Map Amendment (Zoning Change) P-ZC2026-0002 / and Development Code
  Amendment P-DCA2026-0003 – City-initiated petitions for consideration of an
  amendment to Title 9 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code, to establish Development
  Code amendments to implement Program 4 (Replacement Housing) and Program 13
  (Development Code Amendments), as identified in the Housing Plan of the City’s 6th
  Cycle (2021-2029) Housing Element and to comply with State housing law. A General
  Plan Amendment and Zoning Map Amendment (Zone Change) are proposed to create
  a low barrier navigation center overlay zone and an emergency shelter residential
  overlay zone as identified in Program 13 of the Housing Element.

  Mayor Bucknum abstaining due to disqualification.

  Community Development Director Larry Longenecker presented the report.

  City Council discussed the item, provided comments and recommended that staff remove
  certain language to the Ordinance regarding the low barrier navigation centers before it is
  approved at the second reading to take place on the October 13th City Council Meeting.

  The following spoke during the Public Hearing:

  Connie Lanzisera, M.V.: Expressed concerns about the language used in the Staff Report and
  recommended the language be made easier to understand for future items.

  The following spoke during the Public Hearing against this item: James Poettgen, M.V., Jason
  Dourgarian, R.S.M., Sal Faso, M.V., Adan Wright, M.V.

  The following spoke during the Public Hearing in support of this item: Robert Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to (1) find
  that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15060, subd. (c)(2), Section 15061, subd. (b)(3), and
  Section 15378 (b)(5); and (2) adopt Resolution 26-41 approving General Plan Amendment
  P-GPA2026-0005.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Bucknum

City Council Minutes  5  September 22, 2026
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to (3)
  introduce Ordinance 26-363 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Mission Viejo approving Zone Map Amendment (Zoning Change) P-ZC2026-0002, and
  Development Code Amendment P-DCA2026-0003, amending Title 9 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code, to establish Development Code amendments to implement Program 4
  (Replacement Housing) and Program 13 (Development Code Amendments), as identified in
  the Housing Plan of the City’s 6th Cycle (2021-2029) Housing Element. A Zoning Map
  Amendment (Zone Change) is proposed to create a low barrier navigation center overlay zone
  and an emergency shelter residential overlay zone as identified in Program 13 of the Housing
  Element.”

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Bucknum

OLD BUSINESS

 11.  Revisions to the City’s Integrated Pest Management Program Guidelines

  Assistant City Manager Jerry Hill presented the report.

  Mayor Bucknum asked for any council questions.

  There were no requests to speak on this item.

  Council Members provided comments.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1)
  receive and file the report and (2) approve revisions to the current Integrated Pest
  Management Program Guidelines.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT: None

 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 12.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received written report.
City Council Minutes  6  September 22, 2026
  13.  Appointment to Fill One Unscheduled Vacancy on the Planning and Transportation
  Commission

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell appointed a new member to the Planning and Transportation
  Commission, Lorrie Lausten, to fill the unscheduled vacancy in his original appointee’s
  position, with the term expiring in January 2027.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to ratify the
  appointment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 Nothing to report.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 Nothing to report.

 OCSD PUBLIC SAFETY UPDATE

 Chief Larson provided an update highlighting recent public safety efforts in Mission Viejo. He
 reported that proactive enforcement by the community services and gang units led to multiple arrests
 in response to significant graffiti vandalism across several parks, effectively stopping further incidents
 due to strong communication between the community, council, and deputies. Chief Larson also
 praised deputies for preventing a potential suicide at Mission Viejo Mall in coordination with Orange
 County Fire. Furthermore, he detailed a successful multi-agency investigation into catalytic converter
 thefts that resulted in five arrests and significant recoveries. He emphasized that these achievements
 demonstrate the critical importance of community partnership in maintaining safety throughout the
 city.

 OCFA PUBLIC SAFETY UPDATE

 Division Chief Mark Backoff introduced himself, sharing his 33 years with OCFA and ties to Mission
 Viejo. He reported 806 city incidents in August, mainly medical aids, and highlighted recent fires
 including a quick-controlled kitchen fire and a larger fire with hoarding conditions causing significant
 damage. He noted participation in the 9/11 Heroes football game and announced upcoming Fire
 Prevention Week focused on battery safety, plus an open house at Fire Station 24 on October 3.

City Council Minutes  7  September 22, 2026
  COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended - AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley highlighted several recent community events. She commended Mission Viejo
High School’s Heroes game and 9/11 anniversary concert, praised the new "Ales and Trails" event
promoting trail enjoyment, and enjoyed the American Bandstand bash with dance lessons and retro
music. She also attended the annual Sergeant Matt Davis remembrance at Matt Davis Park, expressing
gratitude to police services for organizing the ceremony and noting the attendance of retired and current
deputies.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch highlighted the successful Oktoberfest night market and upcoming lake event,
thanked the city for supporting Saddleback Scout Fest, and shared his recent trip to Washington, D.C.,
where he advocated for Orange County’s transportation and security needs ahead of the 2028 LA
Olympics, stressing the importance of recognizing OC’s role in hosting key events.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez recapped attending several community events and mentioned plans for a refuge
lane and a new e-bike ordinance. She highlighted a potential grant for playground equipment at La
Mancha Park and shared insights from her recent Washington, D.C. advocacy trip on data centers and
infrastructure grants. She also met with multiple federal offices and shared that her daughter recently
joined a sorority.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Nothing to report.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum praised Mission Viejo High School’s Heroes event and the successful Ales and Trails
event. She highlighted a chamber roundtable with an upcoming auto dealership incentive, noted the
city’s July 4th celebrations shared at the Orange County Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast, and mentioned
recent and upcoming community events like Movies in the Park and e-waste collection. She also shared
plans for a trip to Washington, D.C., and encouraged residents to enjoy Restaurant Week.

City Council Minutes  8  September 22, 2026
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:40 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Steven Kramer, beloved SCOR volunteer.

 Alison Walker
 City Clerk

City Council Minutes  9  September 22, 2026
